# Call trees

Generated by `codespec-docs`: the `envcheck` tree is `codespec trace` run now over [`examples/envcheck/envcheck.read.cir.json`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/examples/envcheck/envcheck.read.cir.json) with [`summaries/go-std.effects.json`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/summaries/go-std.effects.json); the `netcheck` trees are read from its checked-in files. `task check` fails when this page drifts from it.

`codespec trace <documents…> --from <path>.<function>` prints `codespec-trace/1`: the call tree from one function over the documents read as one program. It answers *what does this call do, and on which branch*, where `codespec effects` answers *what may it do at all*. Calls are resolved as `codespec effects` resolves them, on the same call graph, with `--from` the only entry for rapid type analysis. The nodes:

| node | what |
|---|---|
| `call` | a call of a function of the set, expanded: the tree of its body; `def` is where it is declared |
| `ref` | a call of a function expanded elsewhere in the tree; each function is expanded once, where it is called fewest calls from `--from` |
| `cut` | a call of a function more than `--depth` calls (default 8) from `--from` |
| `dispatch` | a call through an interface or a function value, each candidate of the set under it |
| `if`, `switch`, `loop` | a branch, with its condition: the `if` condition, the `switch` tag and each case's values, the loop condition or its `range` |
| `syscall` | a syscall the barrier names, with its effects |
| `extern` | a call outside the set (or `println`) with the effects its summary states; `pure` is `[]` |
| `unknown` | a reason the tree may be incomplete there, as `codespec effects` lists it |
| `lambda` | a function literal, with the tree of its body |

A call's arguments are evaluated before it, so calls in one statement appear in evaluation order: `println(Banner(…))` lists `Banner` before `println`.

## `envcheck.Announce`

[`envcheck`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/tree/main/examples/envcheck) prints a banner built from the environment ([`examples/envcheck/source/envcheck.go`](https://github.com/beyond10x/codespec/blob/main/examples/envcheck/source/envcheck.go)). `Announce` calls `Banner`, which calls `Mode` and `Label`; `Mode` reads `APP_MODE` and branches on it being empty. Without the standard library in the set, `os.Getenv` and the `strings` functions are leaves with the effects `summaries/go-std.effects.json` states.

```text title="codespec trace examples/envcheck/envcheck.read.cir.json --summaries summaries/go-std.effects.json --from envcheck.Announce"
envcheck.Announce  envcheck.go:31
├─ envcheck.Banner  envcheck.go:32
│  ├─ envcheck.Mode  envcheck.go:27
│  │  ├─ os.Getenv [env]  envcheck.go:13
│  │  ├─ strings.TrimSpace [pure]  envcheck.go:13
│  │  ├─ if m == ""  envcheck.go:14
│  │  └─ strings.ToUpper [pure]  envcheck.go:17
│  └─ envcheck.Label  envcheck.go:27
│     ├─ strings.ToLower [pure]  envcheck.go:22
│     └─ strconv.Itoa [pure]  envcheck.go:22
└─ println [stdout]  envcheck.go:32
```
## `netcheck` {#netcheck}

[`netcheck`](/docs/examples/netcheck) is a TCP server and client read with every package they import, the standard library included, so its trees end in syscalls. `codespec trace` cannot run here without that set; these trees are the checked-in output of `task examples-netcheck`.

### The client, 2 calls deep

`CheckAll` passes a function literal to the generic `Count`; the literal calls `Prober.Probe`, a `dispatch` node with one candidate under `rta`. `Count` calls its function value `ok`, a `dispatch` node with no candidate: a value of a generic signature is `unknown`. `fmt.Println` writes through `io.Writer.Write`, which may reach every `Write` of the set that code reached from `main` makes.

```text title="examples/netcheck/client.trace.json"
example.com/netcheck/cmd/client.main  main.go:11
├─ example.com/netcheck.TCP  main.go:12
├─ example.com/netcheck.CheckAll  main.go:12
│  ├─ func literal  netcheck.go:78
│  │  └─ dispatch example.com/netcheck.Prober.Probe  netcheck.go:78  (1 candidates)
│  │     └─ example.com/netcheck.TCPProber.Probe  netcheck.go:78
│  │        ├─ net.Dial  netcheck.go:29  (cut: deeper than the depth)
│  │        ├─ if err != nil  netcheck.go:30
│  │        ├─ io.WriteString  netcheck.go:33  (cut: deeper than the depth)
│  │        ├─ if werr != nil  netcheck.go:34
│  │        │  └─ dispatch net.Conn.Close  netcheck.go:35  (1 candidates)
│  │        │     └─ net.conn.Close  netcheck.go:35  (cut: deeper than the depth)
│  │        ├─ bufio.NewReader  netcheck.go:38  (cut: deeper than the depth)
│  │        ├─ bufio.Reader.ReadString  netcheck.go:38  (cut: deeper than the depth)
│  │        ├─ dispatch net.Conn.Close  netcheck.go:39  (1 candidates)
│  │        │  └─ net.conn.Close  netcheck.go:39  (cut: deeper than the depth)
│  │        └─ example.com/netcheck.Answer  netcheck.go:40  (cut: deeper than the depth)
│  └─ example.com/netcheck.Count  netcheck.go:78
│     └─ loop _, x := range xs  netcheck.go:68
│        ├─ dispatch func value func(T) bool  netcheck.go:69  (0 candidates)
│        │  └─ unknown: function value with no candidate in the set: func(T) bool
│        └─ if ok(x)  netcheck.go:69
├─ strconv.Itoa  main.go:13
│  └─ internal/strconv.Itoa  number.go:215
│     └─ internal/strconv.FormatInt  itoa.go:53  (cut: deeper than the depth)
├─ println [stdout]  main.go:13
└─ fmt.Println  main.go:13

      │  ├─ net.conn.Write  print.go:298  (cut: deeper than the depth)
      │  ├─ net.netFD.Write  print.go:298  (cut: deeper than the depth)
      │  ├─ os.File.Write  print.go:298  (cut: deeper than the depth)
```

### The client to `connect`

`codespec trace --from example.com/netcheck/cmd/client.main --depth 16`, pruned to the branches that end in that syscall: every other node is left out, so the tree reads as one path from the entry down to the barrier. Each function is expanded once, where it is fewest calls from the entry. The path to `connect` therefore runs through `dialUDP`: `net.internetSocket` is one call under it and three under the TCP branch (`dialTCP`, `doDialTCP`, `doDialTCPProto`), which holds a `ref` to it.

```text title="examples/netcheck/client-connect.trace.json"
example.com/netcheck/cmd/client.main  main.go:11
└─ example.com/netcheck.CheckAll  main.go:12
   └─ func literal  netcheck.go:78
      └─ dispatch example.com/netcheck.Prober.Probe  netcheck.go:78  (1 candidates)
         └─ example.com/netcheck.TCPProber.Probe  netcheck.go:78
            └─ net.Dial  netcheck.go:29
               └─ net.Dialer.Dial  dial.go:475
                  └─ net.Dialer.DialContext  dial.go:508
                     └─ net.sysDialer.dialParallel  dial.go:560
                        └─ net.sysDialer.dialSerial  dial.go:661
                           └─ net.sysDialer.dialSingle  dial.go:760
                              └─ net.sysDialer.dialUDP  dial.go:799
                                 └─ net.internetSocket  udpsock_posix.go:220
                                    └─ net.socket  ipsock_posix.go:173
                                       └─ net.netFD.dial  sock_posix.go:67
                                          └─ if raddr != nil  sock_posix.go:117
                                             └─ net.netFD.connect  sock_posix.go:121
                                                └─ dispatch func value func(int, syscall.Sockaddr) error  fd_unix.go:47  (1 candidates)
                                                   └─ syscall.Connect  fd_unix.go:47
                                                      └─ syscall.connect  syscall_unix.go:300
                                                         └─ syscall connect [net]  zsyscall_linux_amd64.go:1422
```
